name: New User: Signup to First Form
description: Complete journey from landing page through account creation to first form creation
primary_user_goal: Create a form that collects data effectively while providing a good respondent experience
business_goal: Convert visitor to registered user with published form (activation)
entry_point: Landing page, template gallery, or referral from existing form
friction_points: Account creation (minimized with social login options)
Template vs blank decision (mitigated by template recommendations)
Question configuration complexity (reduced by smart defaults)
Understanding one-at-a-time paradigm (resolved through preview)
success_metrics: Return to edit after first responses
notes: Typeform's activation flow emphasizes experiencing the product as a respondent before building. Many users first encounter Typeform by filling out someone else's form and thinking 'I want my forms to work like this.' The template gallery accelerates time-to-value by providing starting points that demonstrate best practices.

name: Template to Published Form
description: Core creation flow from selecting a template through customization to sharing
primary_user_goal: Transform a template into a personalized, branded form ready for distribution
business_goal: Deliver value that drives form completion and return usage
exit_point: Shared or embedded form collecting responses
friction_points: Adapting template to specific needs (solved by flexible editing)
Configuring logic without confusion (solved by visual flow)
Matching brand aesthetics (solved by theme system)
Choosing distribution method (solved by clear share options)
notes: This is Typeform's core product loop. Templates provide structure while customization creates ownership. The flow is optimized to get forms published quickly - a form collecting responses is more valuable than a perfect form never shared. Preview functionality lets builders experience their form as respondents will.

name: Advanced Form: Logic and Personalization
description: Building sophisticated forms with conditional logic, calculations, and personalization
primary_user_goal: Create intelligent forms that adapt to respondent answers
business_goal: Drive upgrades through advanced feature usage; enable complex use cases
exit_point: Logic-enabled form with tested conditional paths
friction_points: Understanding logic jump concept (solved by visual flowchart)
Testing all paths work correctly (solved by preview with logic)
Calculator formula syntax (solved by helper and examples)
Hidden field configuration (solved by clear documentation)
notes: Logic features are key upgrade drivers and competitive differentiators. The visual flowchart makes complex branching understandable. Natural language conditions (not programming) make logic accessible to non-technical users. Calculator feature enables lead scoring, quizzes with calculated results, and ROI calculators.

name: Respondent: Form Completion
description: End user experience of filling out a Typeform
primary_user_goal: Complete form quickly and without frustration
business_goal: Maximize completion rate and response quality
entry_point: Form link, embedded form, or QR code scan
exit_point: Thank you screen with optional redirect
friction_points: Initial engagement (solved by welcome screen)
Form length anxiety (solved by progress indicator)
Input confusion (solved by clear question types)
Abandonment temptation (solved by engaging experience)
notes: The respondent experience IS Typeform's product. Every design decision serves completion rates. One-at-a-time reduces cognitive load. Keyboard navigation creates flow state. Progress indicators prevent abandonment. Smooth animations make the experience feel crafted, not clinical. This is why Typeform can charge premium pricing - they optimize for the respondent, not just the builder.

name: Analyze and Export Results
description: Reviewing collected responses and extracting insights
primary_user_goal: Understand what responses reveal and take action on insights
business_goal: Demonstrate data value; drive continued usage and upgrades for analytics
exit_point: Exported data or connected integration action
friction_points: Finding specific responses (solved by filtering)
Understanding aggregate patterns (solved by visualizations)
Identifying drop-off causes (solved by funnel analysis)
Getting data into other tools (solved by integrations)
notes: Results analysis closes the value loop. Users see the impact of their form design choices through completion rates and drop-off analysis. This drives iteration - users return to improve forms based on data. Integrations (Zapier, HubSpot, Slack, Google Sheets) turn responses into workflows, embedding Typeform deeper into business processes.

name: Free to Paid Upgrade
description: Conversion journey from free user to paying subscriber
primary_user_goal: Access features needed for current use case
business_goal: Convert free users to recurring revenue
entry_point: Feature limit hit, upgrade prompt, or pricing page
friction_points: Uncertainty about which tier (solved by feature comparison)
Price sensitivity (solved by response volume framing)
Commitment anxiety (solved by monthly option)
Payment friction (solved by standard checkout)
success_metrics: Tier distribution (Basic vs Plus vs Business)
notes: Typeform's upgrade triggers are well-designed. Free tier is useful but naturally limited for serious use. Question and response limits are the primary triggers for casual users. Logic and branding are triggers for professionals. The 'Plus' tier is positioned as the sweet spot. Enterprise features (SSO, compliance) drive larger contracts.
